say: Every product has features. A feature is a fact about it. For example, this shea butter is unrefined.

panel.heading: Connect what it is to why she wants it

cards.d: A fact about the product. Shea butter is unrefined.
What the feature does for her. It keeps its natural moisturising quality.
The real reason she is shopping. Her child has dry skin in harmattan.

say: A benefit is what that feature does for the person. Unrefined shea butter keeps its natural moisturising quality.

panel.heading: Connect what it is to why she wants it

cards.d: A fact about the product. Shea butter is unrefined.
What the feature does for her. It keeps its natural moisturising quality.
The real reason she is shopping. Her child has dry skin in harmattan.

say: A need is the real reason she is shopping. Perhaps her child has dry skin in harmattan.
People buy to meet needs. Features only matter when you connect them to that need.

say: Most buying decisions come down to four questions, even if she never says them aloud. First, need. Without it, good price and trust will not produce a sale.

panel.heading: Four things every customer weighs
items: Need: does this solve my problem now?
Value: is the price fair for what I get?
Trust: will this seller deliver and help me?
Convenience: can I buy and pay without stress?

say: Second, value. Is the price fair compared with other options she knows? Price is only one part of value.

panel.heading: Four things every customer weighs
items: Need: does this solve my problem now?

Trust: will this seller deliver and help me?
Convenience: can I buy and pay without stress?

say: Third, trust. Will you deliver what you promised, and help her if something goes wrong?

say: Fourth, convenience. Can she buy, pay and receive it easily?
Many customers pay a little more to a seller who answers quickly and delivers on time.

say: Here is why this matters in money. Ngozi sells pap and moi moi from a stall in Enugu. An office worker, Chika, buys breakfast from her on most working days.

card.title: What one loyal customer is worth

say: Chika spends about 1,200 naira each visit. She comes about 4 days a week, so that is about 4,800 naira a week.

card.title: What one loyal customer is worth

say: Over about 48 working weeks, that is about 230,400 naira in a year.

card.title: What one loyal customer is worth

say: If Chika also brings two colleagues who each spend half as much, that adds about 230,400 naira more.
One badly handled day, with cold food, a rude reply or wrong change, could lose all of this.

card.title: What one loyal customer is worth

say: Active listening means paying full attention to understand her, not just waiting for your turn to speak.
Habit one, attend. Put your phone down and face her. On WhatsApp, read the whole message and listen to the whole voice note before you reply.

panel.heading: Active listening in four habits
items: Attend: phone down, face her, read the whole message
Ask: open questions about situation, reason, budget, timing
Reflect: repeat the key point in your own words
Summarise and confirm: check you have it right

say: Habit two, ask. Use open questions that begin with what, how, who or when. Instead of asking, do you want a cake, ask, what kind of celebration are you planning?

panel.heading: Active listening in four habits
items: Attend: phone down, face her, read the whole message

say: Habit three, reflect. Repeat back the key point, including feelings. So you have guests coming on Saturday and you are worried the food will not be enough.

say: Habit four, summarise and confirm. Gather the details and ask, is that correct?

say: The common mistake is talking about your products before you understand the customer. Ask first, talk second.

say: Trust also means handling money safely. Fake transfer alerts are a common trick. Screenshots and text messages can be faked.

say: Be careful when a buyer rushes you or sends a screenshot instead of waiting. Never skip the bank app check, however friendly the customer is.

panel.rule: Only money you can see in your own bank app is proof.

say: State the full price and terms in writing before she pays. Her number and address are personal data, so collect only what you need, ask before adding her to a broadcast list, and never share her number.
Meet buyers in busy public places. And if there is a delay, tell her before the deadline, not after.

panel.heading: Trust habits every seller needs
items: Full price and terms in writing before she pays
Collect only the data you need
Ask before adding her to a broadcast list
Never share or sell customer numbers
Meet buyers in busy public places
Promise a realistic time, warn early of delays

say: To remember. People buy to meet needs. They weigh need, value, trust and convenience. Listen before you recommend. Only money in your own app is proof of payment.
And unhappy customers usually leave quietly, so notice who has gone quiet.
